findings.text: The zero-cost half of the previous round's blocking finding is repaired (line 560 routes a zero spend through BudgetManager.record_llm_cost_event without reserving), but the other half survives: when manager.reserve returns None the sink returns at line 565 and the call the provider already billed leaves no LLMCost row and no release, which is the silent loss the change exists to end. Recording with overspend, as BudgetLease.charge_event's short-pool path already does at imas_codex/standard_names/budget.py:596, would keep the row.

The tests: line and both baseline_suite/after_suite commands select tests/core, tests/discovery/test_llm_decisions.py, tests/discovery/test_judgment.py and tests/standard_names, which collect zero items from tests/discovery/test_decisions_release_tracking.py — the node's own fifteen tests — so the recorded gate cannot redden on a regression in the change it measures; gate-release-zero.log runs them separately at 15 passed EXIT=0 but carries no revision header, and the after_suite revision is 73acefa34, three commits behind the reviewed head.

The fragment points a reader at 'the sibling fragment's pricing-reference-grep.txt' for the pricing scan, and no such file exists in the repository at 77e08fcdb or in the run directory, so the evidence for leaving the three pricing rows in place cannot be opened by the reader who needs it.

The commits: field lists ten shas while git log 6c73f1747..77e08fcdb returns fifteen, omitting 6f5564b9d, 7c0bfd269, 566ee7678, 737edff17 and 393caa869, so a coordinator reconciling the landed change against the record sees two thirds of it.

openrouter-pricing rows for openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna (:904), gpt-5.5 (:952) and gpt-5.4 (:963) remain, so the done-when's literal 'pyproject.toml references no OpenAI model older than the newest of its tier' is unmet; leaving them is the right call because tests/ still name those ids and an unpriced model fails closed, but the guard added at tests/core/test_settings.py:607 asserts the slate and the route table and never the pricing section, so a stale row would not redden it.
